properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued November 21 at 10:28PM EST until November 21 at 10:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
At 1028 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located near the Saint Lucie Nuclear Power Plant, moving
northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

Locations impacted include...
Walton, Saint Lucie Nuclear Power Plant, Nettles Island, Indian
River Estates and Hutchinson Island South.
properties.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 22 at 8:47PM EST until November 23 at 11:00AM EST by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Lake effect snow expected. Total snow accumulations between
2 and 5 inches. Up to 8 inches underneath the dominant lake effect
snow band.

* WHERE...Baraga, Northern Houghton, Ontonagon, and Southern Houghton
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM EST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. Moderate to heavy
snowfall rates will cause visibility to fall below 1 mile at times.
The hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A dominant lake effect band with heavy
snowfall rates up to 1 inch per hour at times will yield an area of
6-8 inches of snow. Medium confidence in exact placement of this
band. Area of focus is between Ontonagon, Painesdale, Herman,
Covington, and Bruce Crossing. Heaviest snowfall expected to remain
south of Houghton.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling.

During lake effect snow, the weather can vary from bands of locally
heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away. Visibilities can
also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in weather,
visibility, and road conditions.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 22 at 2:01PM AST until November 22 at 5:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
FFWSJU

The National Weather Service in San Juan has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Bayamon...Catano...Guaynabo and Toa Baja...

* Until 500 PM AST.

* At 201 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area, including northern
Guaynabo and northern Bayamon. Up to 3 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sabana Seca, Catano, Guaynabo, Levittown and Ingenio.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
properties.areaDesc: Bayamon, PR; Catano, PR; Guaynabo, PR; Toa Baja, PR
